source.title: Stronger Convergence Results for Deep Residual Networks: Network Width Scales Linearly with Training Data Size

record.tranche_reason: The paper proves a convergence result for a residual network with quadratic loss and arbitrary labels, which bears on fitting random labels, but it does not run the original empirical intervention.
record.gate_note: The introduction's statement that gradient descent can achieve zero training loss even for random labels cites Zhang et al. [5] and is not this study's result. The study's own theorem concerns convergence for arbitrary labels under stated assumptions.
record.test_reason: Theorem 6.1 proves convergence to arbitrarily small training residual for arbitrary labels, including random labels, under specified ResNet assumptions. This bears on V1's fitting component through a theoretical method.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: under the stated assumptions, the authors establish linear convergence of full gradient descent with a width bound proportional to sample size and independent of depth, conditional on the data-dependent constants. They leave stochastic-gradient and test-loss analyses for future work.
record.recipe_differences: A theoretical convergence analysis of a defined ResNet with full gradient descent, quadratic loss, and a linear width bound; no empirical reproduction of the original random-label experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The result requires the paper's ResNet setup, quadratic loss, smooth activation assumptions, unit-norm inputs, stated initialization and step-size bound, and width at least Kδ,δ′ n.
record.peer_reviewed: Information and Inference: A Journal of the IMA
record.problems: The result is theoretical and conditional; there is no random-label experiment, stochastic-gradient result, or test-loss/generalization result. The paper identifies stochastic gradient analysis and test-loss analysis as future work.
record.rows_left_out: No additional own results on the claim were reported. The introduction's random-label statement cites prior work [5], so it is not extracted as a result row.

untested.parts: Stochastic-gradient training, chance test error, and fitting random versus true labels without changing architecture or hyperparameters are not evaluated. The proof concerns full gradient descent, quadratic loss, and the specified smooth-activation ResNet.
No comparison of fitting times for true and random labels or convergence across corruption fractions.
No results specifically establishing fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
No corruption-fraction sweep or test-error degradation result.
No comparisons involving weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, or generalization after removing regularization.
No analysis comparing when real patterns and noisy labels are learned.

record.verdict_notes: The theorem's sufficient conditions do not show that fitting fails outside those conditions, so they do not warrant limits_scope. Unmeasured components likewise do not warrant limits_scope. The introduction's empirical random-label statement is attributed to prior work.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label experiment, test error, stochastic-gradient experiment, or comparison with training on true labels. The result is conditional on the paper's ResNet, smooth activation, quadratic loss, and width bound.

rows.subject: ResNet model as defined in (2.3)
rows.size_stated: width m ≥ Kδ,δ′ n; depth H = H(δ′, B, cres) sufficiently large and independent of m or n
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical gradient descent convergence result for quadratic loss, under the theorem's initialization, width, step-size, and data assumptions; labels y are arbitrary.

conditions.value: bounded first and second derivatives; also |φ(a + b)| ≤ |φ(a)| + |φ(b)|
weight matrices have i.i.d. N(0, 1) entries

rows.measure: Training residual convergence under gradient descent
rows.value: ∥fres(θτ) − y∥²₂ ≤ (1 − ηα²δ′/2)τ ∥fres(θ0) − y∥²₂; the paper states convergence to the globally optimal solution.
rows.uncertainty: Probability at least 1 − κ1 m e^(−κ2 mδ) − H e^(−m²/2) − e^(−δ²n/(2∥X∥²)) − ∑(k=1 to H−1)e^(−δ²n/(2∥X(k)∥²)).
rows.note: The theorem is for arbitrary label vector y, so it covers random labels as a mathematical case, but does not instantiate random labels or report a test error. It analyzes gradient descent, not stochastic gradient descent.
rows.check: The bound establishes complete asymptotic fitting under its assumptions; partial is inappropriate merely because other parts of V1 are untested. Add the fixed output vector: half its entries are +||y||₂/√n and half are −||y||₂/√n. The width bound requires positive λ(X) and depends on this data-dependent quantity; linear width scaling is conditional on that dependence.

relationships.condition: Training-set fitting under Theorem 6.1's smooth ResNet, quadratic-loss, initialization, positive-kernel-eigenvalue, width, depth, and step-size assumptions
relationships.reason: R1 proves geometric decay of training residual to zero for arbitrary label vectors, which includes completely random labels; this supports the fitting component within the theorem's setting.
relationships.display_finding: Training residual decays geometrically to zero for arbitrary label vectors, including completely random assignments.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The theorem gives convergence for arbitrary labels, but only conditionally for its specified ResNet, quadratic loss, smooth activation, and width regime; it does not test the stated random-label setting or test error (R1).
